chunks: Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn Mahbub narrated from al-'Abbas ibn Ma'ruf, from 'Abd Allah ibn al-Mughirah, from Dharih, from Abu 'Abd Allah عليه السلام, who said:
Abu Sa'id al-Khudri was mentioned, so he said: “He was among the companions of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, and he was upright.”
He said: “Then he remained in the throes for three days, and his family washed him, then carried him to his place of prayer, and he died in it.”

He said: “When you direct the deceased toward the qiblah, then turn his face toward the qiblah; do not place him crosswise as people do. For indeed I saw our companions doing that, although Abu Basir used to command placing him crosswise; 'Ali ibn Abi Hamzah informed me of that.”
He said: “Then when the deceased dies, proceed with his preparation and hasten it.”

key_terms.أَصْحَابَنَا: the companions or associates of the Imam عليه السلام whose practice is cited
key_terms.الْقِبْلَةِ: the direction of prayer toward which the deceased should be oriented
key_terms.الْمَيِّتَ: the deceased person whose body is being prepared after death
key_terms.جَهَازِهِ: the funeral preparation and arrangement of the deceased
key_terms.عَجِّلْهُ: hasten it, meaning do not delay the funeral arrangements
key_terms.مُعْتَرِضًا: placed crosswise or sideways rather than facing properly toward the qiblah

ai.seo_question: How should a deceased person be turned toward the qiblah and how quickly should funeral preparations be made in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith discusses matters related to the dying person and the deceased, including how the body should be directed toward the qiblah and the importance of hastening funeral preparations. It also includes a brief mention of Abu Sa'id al-Khudri and reports the practice observed among the companions of the Imam عليه السلام regarding positioning the deceased.
